title: Daily AI & Tech News Brief
summary: Concise AI, mobile, consumer-device, cybersecurity, and open-source technology news summaries with source links.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Tag as a Slack-native AI coworker
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Tag, a beta agentic assistant for Claude Team and Enterprise customers that works inside Slack, learns workspace context, and can suggest or coordinate follow-up work.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-5 Pro helped solve a long-running immunology mystery
items.summary: OpenAI published a case study describing how GPT-5 Pro helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz reason through a three-year T cell research problem, pointing to possible uses in cancer and autoimmune research workflows.

items.title: Hugging Face and IBM Research show CUGA examples for agentic apps
items.summary: A new Hugging Face post from IBM Research demonstrates CUGA with two dozen working examples for building agentic applications on a lightweight harness, useful for developers evaluating practical agent patterns.

items.title: OSI announces an Open Source AI Fellowship at UN Open Source Week
items.summary: The Open Source Initiative announced an Open Source AI Fellowship during UN Open Source Week, extending its work around open AI definitions, policy, and community governance.

items.title: Fake AI agent skill reportedly passed security scans and reached 26,000 agents
items.summary: The Hacker News reports that security firm AIR placed a fake AI-agent skill through marketplace and ad channels, where it allegedly passed tested scanners and reached about 26,000 agents, highlighting supply-chain risks for agent ecosystems.

items.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that could enable code execution
items.summary: Microsoft patched an AutoGen Studio vulnerability chain nicknamed AutoJack that could let a malicious webpage manipulate an AI agent into running commands on its host system.

items.title: Scattered Spider hackers plead guilty in UK Transport for London case
items.summary: KrebsOnSecurity reports that two men linked to the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty on the first day of trial over the 2024 attack that disrupted Transport for London.

items.title: OpenAI launches Patch the Planet for open-source security fixes
items.summary: OpenAI announced Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative that will help open-source maintainers find, validate, and fix security vulnerabilities using AI plus expert review. The program is notable because it connects agentic AI work with practical software-supply-chain security.

items.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that allowed command execution
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that Microsoft fixed an AutoGen Studio vulnerability chain called AutoJack. The issue could let a malicious webpage manipulate an AI agent workflow into running commands on the host, underlining why agent tooling needs strong sandboxing and prompt-boundary defenses.

items.title: Canada used a first-of-its-kind warrant to clean botnet-infected devices
items.summary: The Hacker News says Canada's spy agency received court authorization to neutralize two foreign-run botnets on infected servers, routers, and IoT devices located in Canada. The case is important because it shows a more active legal model for disrupting compromised infrastructure.

items.title: Hugging Face highlights PP-OCRv6 for multilingual OCR
items.summary: Hugging Face published a post on PP-OCRv6, a family of OCR models covering 50 languages with sizes from 1.5M to 34.5M parameters. It is useful for developers who need document, image-text, or creator-tool pipelines that can run with smaller OCR models.

items.title: Qwen posts a Qwen Image Bench repository on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now lists Qwen-Image-Bench, a repository related to image benchmarking. It is a model-listing signal rather than a full launch post, but it is relevant for tracking Qwen's multimodal evaluation ecosystem.
